tagline: The largest of the Princes' Islands — no cars, horse-drawn carriages, Victorian mansions, and the most beautiful escape from Istanbul.

items.name: Yücetepe Kır Gazinosu
items.description: A historic garden café near the top of the island with views across the Sea of Marmara. Worth the uphill walk or carriage ride.
items.tip: Order the island breakfast and take your time. There is genuinely no rush on Büyükada.

items.name: İskele Meydanı Kafeler
items.description: Cafés and tea houses right at the ferry landing with views of arriving boats and the island's Victorian mansions. Perfect for the first coffee of the day.

items.name: Büyükada Balık Restoranları
items.description: Several excellent fish restaurants near the harbour serving fresh Marmara catch. The setting — sea air, no cars, the sound of horse carriages — is unlike anywhere else.

items.name: Ada Pastaneleri
items.description: The island has wonderful traditional pastry shops selling island-style börek, gözleme, and sweets. Perfect for a picnic on the hills.
items.tip: Buy your picnic supplies at the bazaar near the ferry landing before heading up the hills.

items.name: Cycling the Island
items.description: Rent a bicycle at the ferry landing and cycle the perimeter road — one of the great simple pleasures of Istanbul. No cars anywhere.
items.tip: The full perimeter takes about 90 minutes at a relaxed pace. The south coast has the best views.

items.name: Aya Yorgi Kilisesi
items.description: A Greek Orthodox monastery at the top of the island's highest hill with extraordinary views. A peaceful pilgrimage for any faith.
items.tip: Walk up or take a horse carriage. Many visitors tie a string along the path up — a traditional wish-making custom.

items.name: Victorian Mansion Walk
items.description: The streets above the ferry landing are lined with ornate 19th-century wooden mansions — Istanbul's finest collection. Just walk and look.

tips: Ferry from Kabataş (45 min) or Bostancı (30 min). Fast ferries also run from Kadıköy. Check İDO and Şehir Hatları for timetables.
There are NO cars on the island — only horse carriages, bicycles, and your own feet. Plan accordingly.
Go on a weekday in spring or autumn. Summer weekends are extremely crowded and the ferry queues can be long.
Bring cash — many small vendors, carriage drivers, and restaurants don't accept cards.
